transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, I guess I’m here because flying has started to feel way scarier than it should. Even just thinking about getting on a plane, I picture this turbulence from my honeymoon flight, and it kind of sticks in my head. Which is frustrating, because I know people fly safely every day—my cousin flies all the time for work, actually, and she acts like it’s nothing—but for me it’s just become this big thing.
Is your fear mainly limited to flying?

Yeah, mainly flying. Like, it’s not that I’m scared of every little thing, it’s just… the idea of getting on a plane now makes me go right back to that honeymoon flight with the turbulence. Which is silly because I know planes are safe—my cousin flies constantly and is totally fine—but my brain just kind of gets stuck on it.
Do unwanted memories of that honeymoon flight ever pop into your mind when you’re not trying to think about it?

I don’t know… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I think about it when something reminds me, like if someone mentions a flight or I see those boarding scenes in a movie. But it’s not like I’m just making dinner and suddenly I’m back there—though, actually, the other day I was making pasta and my husband brought up vacation ideas, and then I started thinking about it. So maybe that’s more the flying thing than the memory just popping in on its own.
When you think about flying, are you mainly afraid that other people will judge you if you get anxious on the plane?

Um… I don’t think that’s the main thing. I mean, I’d be embarrassed if I was visibly freaking out, sure, because nobody wants to be that person on a plane, you know? But it’s not really about people judging me. It’s more just the flying itself that gets in my head.

Like, I work around parents and staff all day, so I’m used to people seeing me stressed sometimes—well, not that I love it, but you know what I mean. On a plane it’s not so much “what will people think,” it’s more… I don’t know, just being on the plane.
Have you avoided flying because of this fear?

Yeah… I have. I mean, I try to make it sound practical, like, “Oh, driving will be cheaper,” or “It’s only, what, nine hours?” which is ridiculous because then we lose a whole day, and my husband is like, “You know we could just fly.” But I’ll pick the long drive if I can.

And for work, there were a couple trainings that would’ve meant flying, and I just kind of… didn’t go. I said the timing wasn’t great, which was partly true, but not really the main reason. Even just talking seriously about a trip, I need my husband sitting there with me or I start backing out and changing the subject.
